section.title: Activity
section.para: An elevator car in a skyscraper can hold at most 15 people. For safety reasons, each car can carry a maximum of 1,500 kg. On average, an adult weighs 70 kg and a child weighs 35 kg. Assume that each person carries 4 kg of gear with them.

div.para: Compare your answer: Your answer may vary, but here are some samples. :

list.item: \( p ≤ 15 \), where \( p \) represents the number of people in an elevator car.
\( a + c ≤ 15 \), where \( a \) represents the number of adults and \( c \) represents the number of children in an elevator car.
\( w ≤ 1,500 \), where \( w \) represents the weight in kilograms in one elevator car.

Write as many equations and inequalities as you can think of to represent the constraints in this situation. Be sure to specify the meaning of any letters that you use. (Avoid using the letters \( z \), \( m \), or \( g \).)
After you have finished the following tasks, explain the adjustments you made to the equations and inequalities so that they are communicated more clearly.

problem.para: Trade your work with a partner and read each other’s equations and inequalities.

list.item: Explain to your partner what you think their statements mean, and listen to their explanation of yours.
Make adjustments to your equations and inequalities so that they are communicated more clearly.

div.para: Compare your answer: Your answer may vary, but here are some samples.

list.item: Rewrite your equations and inequalities so that they would work for a different building where:
an elevator car can hold at most \( z \) people
each car can carry a maximum of \( m \) kilograms
each person carries \( d \) kg of gear
